# Tidecoin

> Post-quantum cryptocurrency using FALCON-512 signatures (NIST-selected; FN-DSA/FIPS 206 in preparation), operational since December 2020.

Tidecoin is an independently maintained post-quantum cryptocurrency derived from
Bitcoin Core. It replaces ECDSA entirely with post-quantum signature schemes.
Every transaction since genesis
(December 27, 2020) has been signed with FALCON-512, a lattice-based scheme selected
by NIST for standardization as FN-DSA (FIPS 206, in preparation). The network has produced over
2.7 million blocks with zero security incidents.

The Tidecoin 1.x codebase was initially based on Bitcoin Core v30 and has since
evolved through Tidecoin-specific development and selected updates from later
Bitcoin Core development. Tidecoin maintains its own releases, consensus rules,
and compatibility requirements.

## Key Facts

- Ticker: TDC
- Genesis: December 27, 2020
- Blocks produced: 2,700,000+
- Security incidents: 0
- Max supply: ~21,000,000 TDC
- Block time: 60 seconds
- Mining: YespowerTIDE (CPU-only, memory-hard)
- Premine/ICO: None
- License: MIT

## Post-Quantum Cryptography

Tidecoin uses NIST-selected post-quantum primitives. ML-DSA and ML-KEM are
finalized NIST standards; Falcon's FN-DSA standard (FIPS 206) is in preparation,
and Tidecoin uses the pinned PQClean implementation of the Falcon Round 3
specification:

- FALCON-512 (FN-DSA/FIPS 206 in preparation): Default signature scheme since genesis. Variable-length compressed signatures without padding, at most 666 bytes when signed locally
- FALCON-1024 (FN-DSA/FIPS 206 in preparation): Higher security variant (post-AuxPoW). Variable-length compressed signatures, at most 1,280 bytes when signed locally
- ML-DSA-44 (FIPS 204): Module-lattice digital signatures (post-AuxPoW), 2,420 bytes
- ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204): Module-lattice digital signatures (post-AuxPoW), 3,309 bytes
- ML-DSA-87 (FIPS 204): Module-lattice digital signatures (post-AuxPoW), 4,627 bytes
- ML-KEM-512 (FIPS 203): Key exchange for opportunistic v2 P2P encryption. Peers can still use unencrypted v1 connections, and the handshake does not verify peer identity
- SHA-512 (FIPS 180-4): Witness script hashing for 256-bit quantum security (post-AuxPoW)

Signature sizes exclude the transaction sighash byte. Falcon's local signing
limits are not consensus length limits. ML-DSA verification requires the exact
fixed length listed for its parameter set.

No ECDSA, Schnorr, or Taproot exists anywhere in the protocol.

## How Tidecoin Compares

| Feature | Tidecoin | QRL | Bitcoin |
|---------|----------|-----|---------|
| PQ since genesis | Yes (Dec 2020) | Yes (Jun 2018) | No |
| Signature scheme | FALCON-512 (NIST) | XMSS (stateful) | ECDSA |
| Signature size | Up to 666 bytes (variable) | ~2,500 bytes | ~71 bytes |
| PQ transport | ML-KEM-512 | No | No |
| Stateless signatures | Yes | No | N/A |
| NIST standard | FIPS 206 in preparation | No | No |
